title: Retro frontmatter
description: The YAML frontmatter of a retro. Every field is here because it CANNOT SURVIVE THE COPY any other way: a retro is what travels from a solution into ai-sdlc's corpus, and git metadata does not travel. The findings and their dispositions live in the body as a markdown table, following the same convention as a spec's criteria and a plan's files.

cycle-id.description: Identity, and the target of caused-by links. Not an indication of completion order: ids are assigned at intent creation and cycles land out of order.

solution.description: Which solution this came from. Partitions the corpus, and aggregation groups by (pack, invariant id) rather than pooling across packs — 'where does our process leak' may have a genuinely different answer for a library than for a competition.

landed-at.description: When the cycle landed. NOT derivable after absorption: ai-sdlc's git date is the date the retro was copied in, while the landing date lives in the solution repository's history, which ai-sdlc does not have.

charter-version.description: The charter in force when the cycle ran. A retro is uninterpretable without it — the amendment analysis asks what changed between versions.

pack-version.description: The stack pack in force, or null for a solution consuming none. Same reason as charter-version, for the half of the rules INV-04 delegates.

outcome.description: A retro exists only for a cycle that landed — its presence IS the completion certificate, which is why a blocked or abandoned cycle writes none.

rounds.description: Interrogation rounds the cycle took. The headline process metric: the finding rate does not decay, so a high count is the normal case rather than a failure.

caused-by.description: For a cycle that fixed something an earlier cycle caused. Accepts `unknown` explicitly: a guessed attribution pollutes the only unbiased signal the loop has, so it must never be forced.

suppression-count.description: Carried forward so the next cycle can detect an increase, which is itself a finding.

allOf.$comment: Naming a stage without naming the cycle names the stage of nothing.
